speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: This includes the newly formed households claiming their CDC vouchers for the first time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: This marked the highest amount and percentage of vouchers claimed compared to all the previous rounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Similar to the 2021 and 2022 vouchers, Singaporean households had the option to help the needy by donating their unused 2023 vouchers before 31 January 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: They could contribute to participating charities that support a range of causes, such as animal welfare, arts and heritage, children and youth, the environment, migrant community, persons with disabilities and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The CDCs will then give the respective charities the cash equivalent of the CDC vouchers that are donated to them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is, most of us understand that the CDC vouchers have been positively received by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State give us the update on the CDC vouchers, in particularly, the Minister of State mentioned just now the claim rate has improved.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But is it as high or better than last year?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What are the drivers, and can it be even higher?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second supplementary question is, since the option for households to donate their CDC vouchers has started, has there been more charities wanting to get on board the list of recipients?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State please provide an update on this?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In my main reply, I mentioned that, in terms of the claim rate for 2023, it is the highest claim rate at 97.7%.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As the Member Mr Saktiandi Supaat mentioned, we are very grateful that the CDC Vouchers Scheme has been widely used and well-received by Singaporean households.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It has been about a month since Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has launched the 2024 CDC Vouchers Scheme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, allow me to just give an update.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It has only been a month, and we all know that Singapore households have a whole year to claim and use the vouchers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But do allow me to give an interim update as of 6 February.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This represent 95% of all Singaporean households, that is, 95% of the 1.27 million Singaporean households.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I can give a further breakdown, but it is really interim because it has only been a month.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the second supplementary question on the donation, allow me to give some background.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The main objective of the CDC Vouchers Scheme, as directed by the Government to us, is to support Singaporean households to use this to defray their household expenses.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But we heard feedback from Singaporean households, especially in 2022.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The CDC Vouchers donation scheme was started then because we received feedback from Singaporeans who wished to donate their unused CDC vouchers to help others in need.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because of that, we started concerted efforts to roll out these options to Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The number of charities has increased steadily since we started this scheme in December 2022.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Back then, the total number of participating charities was about 270.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As of today, 327 charities are on board and that represents about a 20% increase in participating charities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to welcome more to come onboard.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They champion various causes, community and social causes, like environment sustainability, animal welfare, arts and heritage, children and youth, the migrant community, and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I must also clarify that these participating charities are Institutions of Public Character.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member also asked for an update on the number of the 2023 vouchers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure him that we will certainly share the number in due course and encourage other participating charities to come on board the donation scheme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The CDC will give the respective charities in the CDC Voucher donation scheme the cash equivalent of the CDC vouchers 2023 that are donated to them.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Any unspent and any undonated vouchers will have to be returned to the Government.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to recap a little for Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I recall one of the top charities that received the most donation is Children's Cancer Foundation – it received an aggregate donation of about $80,000.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, even as the CDC Vouchers Scheme is designed to support all Singaporean households to defray their household expenses, their expenses on daily necessities and essential services, I think it has also served a secondary purpose of doing good, especially for Singaporeans who want to donate their CDC vouchers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The top three charity sectors that received the highest donation amounts for the 2021 to 2022 vouchers, are, first, the healthcare-related charities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The second category is the families and children's charities; and the third category is the youth and children's charities.
